title: Uzbek Nationalism
abstract: Modern Uzbek nationalism builds itself on Uzbek traditions, Islam and the Jadids, and its textbooks paint Soviet Uzbekistan as a red colony. Starting from a classroom quarrel with a teacher who wished Russia would take Uzbekistan back, this essay argues that the history of Central Asia cannot be read as a story of good Central Asians and bad Russians, and still concludes that the Russian Empire has no place in the twenty-first century.

title: Gapirma!
abstract: The state may monitor us through documentation and technology, while society has always monitored us through gossip. From Soviet walls that listened to the mahalla's g‘iybat and mishmish, this essay asks whether privacy, as we once understood it, ever existed at all.
